title: Machine-Learning-Empowered Quantum Sensing of the Plaquette Phase in a Three-Level Delta System
authors: Lorenzo Vitale, Shreyasi Mukherjee, Dario Fasone, Enrico Martello, Elisabetta Paladino, Luigi Giannelli, Giuseppe Falci
abstract: We propose a machine-learning-empowered approach to the quantum sensing of the plaquette phase, a gauge-invariant quantity arising in three-level $Δ$ systems. This phase profoundly affects the system dynamics, breaking coherent population trapping and inducing a non-trivial phase dependence of the dynamics. We demonstrate that a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), trained in a supervised-learning framework, can accurately estimate the plaquette phase from STImulated Raman Adiabatic Passage (STIRAP) population transfer efficiencies measured under different driving conditions, which provide experimentally accessible observables. Our results highlight how the combination of coherent control and machine learning (ML) enables effective phase identification in closed-loop quantum systems, opening new perspectives for quantum technologies, specifically quantum sensing applications including synthetic gauge fields.
summary: The research proposes using machine learning to sense the plaquette phase in a three-level atomic system by analyzing how this unknown phase perturbs STIRAP population transfer efficiencies. By training an MLP on simulated data, the authors demonstrate that these accessible quantum control measurements encode enough information to accurately reconstruct the underlying gauge-invariant phase.
main_problem: The paper addresses the quantum sensing of the plaquette phase ($\phi$) within a three-level $\Delta$ system, which is a gauge-invariant quantity affecting system dynamics.
main_result: A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) trained on simulated STIRAP population transfer efficiencies can accurately reconstruct the unknown plaquette phase with high fidelity.
method: The methodology involves framing the problem as an inverse mapping, using supervised machine learning to predict $\phi$ from multiple measured quantum control observables.
model_or_system: The system is a three-level $\Delta$-type atomic configuration described by a Hamiltonian that includes the unknown plaquette phase. The dynamics are probed using Stimulated Raman Adiabatic Passage (STIRAP) protocols.
key_observables: Stimulated Raman Adiabatic Passage (STIRAP) population transfer efficiencies ($\eta$), which depend non-trivially on the plaquette phase $\phi$.
important_parameters: The plaquette phase $\phi$, system coupling strengths ($\Omega_0, \Omega_p, \Omega_s$), and detuning parameters.
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the STIRAP efficiency measurements provide sufficient information to uniquely determine the unknown gauge-invariant phase $\phi$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three-level system setup; one shows the dependence of STIRAP efficiency on $\phi$, and later figures demonstrate the convergence and test performance of the MLP model in reconstructing the true phase.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and the concept of the plaquette phase. It then details how this phase breaks Coherent Population Trapping (CPT) and influences STIRAP dynamics. The core is the development and training of an MLP using simulated data derived from these dynamic measurements to achieve phase estimation.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, modern example of leveraging machine learning in quantum physics—specifically turning a difficult-to-measure physical parameter (a gauge phase) into a measurable diagnostic signal via controlled dynamics.
